references.text: Both texts express God's desire that his people would listen and walk in his ways, with a focus on wisdom and understanding.
Isaiah expresses a similar thought that the people should have paid attention to God's commands to attain peace, a parallel to understanding their future.
Jeremiah asks who is wise enough to understand why the land is going to ruin, which connects to the theme of wisdom and understanding consequences.
Hosea calls on the wise to understand the Lord's ways, reflecting the call for wisdom and insight into one's destiny.
Moses speaks of wisdom and understanding being visible to the nations, connecting to the desire that Israel would be wise.
Proverbs teaches that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, which is the foundation for the wisdom that Deuteronomy seeks.
Jesus weeps over Jerusalem because they did not understand what made for their peace, a direct parallel to failing to understand their destiny.
